newsitem.title: UK: CE confident of full Northern control.
newsitem.headline: CE confident of full Northern control.

text.p: CE Electric is confident that it will win full control of British power supplier Northern Elecric Plc, a source close to the U.S. company said on Tuesday.
On Monday Northern effectively conceded defeat in a close-fought battle for its independence when it advised all shareholders to accept CE's 650 pence per share offer.

After CE Electric narrowly won 50.3 percent of Northern's shares on Christmas Eve there was speculation that a clutch of institutions grouped around Prudential Corp might hold out as minority shareholders. Prudential bought 700,000 Northern shares on December 24 in a last-ditch attempt to thwart CE.
CE, which is controlled by CalEnergy Co Inc, needs to win 90 percent of Northern to be able to buy the remaining 10 percent compulsorily.
A Cal Energy source told Reuters: "It doesn't make any sense to sit as a minority shareholder with a very illiquid stock. The purchaser is in a much stronger position."
He added that "acceptances are beginning to come in", but official disclosures would not be forthcoming until "significant" blocks of shares had been surrendered.

The three major institutional investors that have been holding out against CE are Prudential, which has argued that the company is worth more than CE's 782 million stg offer, M&G Group Plc and Foreign & Colonial, which manages Northern's pension fund.
A spokesman for Foreign & Colonial said: "We have decided on our course of action, but we don't wish to make it public."
Neither Prudential, which holds just over 12 percent of Northern, nor M&G were immediately available for comment.
